name: 1Password CLI
description: Protects against destructive 1Password CLI operations like deleting items, \ documents, users, groups, and vaults.

destructive_patterns.name: op-item-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op item delete removes secret items (including archive operations).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a 1Password item permanently removes the secret (passwords, API keys, \ credentials). Without --archive, this cannot be undone. Applications and users \ relying on this item will lose access to the stored credentials.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op item get: Export item fields before deletion \ - op item delete --archive: Move to archive for recovery \ - Verify no applications reference this item

destructive_patterns.name: op-document-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op document delete removes secure documents (including archive operations).
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a 1Password document permanently removes the file (certificates, keys, \ configurations). Unlike items, documents may contain unique binary data that \ cannot be recreated from memory.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op document get: Download document before deletion \ - op document delete --archive: Move to archive for recovery \ - Back up to secure local storage first

destructive_patterns.name: op-vault-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op vault delete removes an entire vault.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a vault removes all items, documents, and permissions within it. This \ affects all users with vault access and any applications using items from this \ vault. This action cannot be undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op item list --vault=X: Inventory vault contents \ - Export items and documents before deletion \ - Move items to a different vault instead

destructive_patterns.name: op-user-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op user delete removes a user from 1Password.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a user revokes their access to all vaults and items. Any private vaults \ owned by the user may be transferred or lost. Service accounts and integrations \ created by this user may also be affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op user suspend: Suspend instead of delete for recovery \ - op user get: Document user permissions first \ - Transfer vault ownership before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: op-group-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op group delete removes a group.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a group removes the permission boundary and all vault assignments. \ Members lose access to vaults shared through this group. This affects team \ organization and access control policies.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op group list: Review group membership first \ - Reassign vault permissions to individual users \ - Create replacement group before deleting old one

destructive_patterns.name: op-connect-token-delete
destructive_patterns.description: op connect token delete revokes access tokens.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Connect token immediately revokes API access for integrations using \ it. CI/CD pipelines, deployment scripts, and applications fetching secrets will \ fail to authenticate until a new token is configured.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - op connect token list: Document token usage first \ - Create new token before deleting old one \ - Update integrations with new token prior to deletion
